question: 9 incoming wire fees went to 7710, but 3 (B-BL-00243, B-BL-00368, B-BL-00370) were booked to 6310 payment processing fees. I treated 7710 as correct. Should those 3 be reclassed?
answer: Yes. Reclass B-BL-00243, B-BL-00368 and B-BL-00370 from 6310 to 7710, because 6310 is only for Paystream fees. Also, there's no $30.00 cap: incoming wire fees on the bank's fee schedule go to 7710 whatever the amount. If any of those three sit in a closed period, send them to me (controller) rather than posting the reclass yourself.

question: Shortfalls as small as 2.46 went to Priya and were cleared to 1200 after 6 to 7 days. Should there be a small-difference write-off limit for staff, or does every unexplained short-pay go to AR?
answer: No, staff don't get a small-difference write-off limit. Every unexplained short-pay goes to the AR lead, even $2.46, and nothing gets written off at any amount without my approval as controller.

question: I see 3 prepayments (150,000 to 400,000), all booked to 2450 the same day by staff. Above 400,000 I send them to the controller. Is that the right limit and the right person?
answer: No, we don't use a dollar limit. A large wire with no invoice goes to 2450 customer deposits only if we have a signed order form email for it, whatever the amount and whether or not it says PREPAY. If there's no signed order form, it goes to ar_lead, not the controller.

question: 4 unmatched customer wires (97,675 to 218,963) were left open, 2 of them pending with Priya. Should wires still unidentified at month end be parked in 1290 unapplied receipts instead of staying open?
answer: Our policy doesn't say anything about parking unidentified wires in 1290 at month end, so don't do that. Bring those wires to me (controller) to decide. Also, your rule is missing a step: if a large wire has no invoice but we have a signed order form email, it goes to 2450 customer deposits. Only wires with no signed order form go to ar_lead.

question: 2 analysis charges went to 7710 and the March one (B-BL-00371, 214.47) went to 6310. Is 7710 correct, and should the March charge be reclassed?
answer: Yes, 7710 is right. Account analysis charges are on the bank's fee schedule, so they go to 7710 at any amount; there's no 234.15 cap. The March charge (B-BL-00371, 214.47) should not be in 6310, which is only for Paystream fees, so reclass it to 7710. If March is already closed, send the reclass entry to me rather than posting it straight into the closed period.

question: I see 2 late accrual true-ups to 6600 for Pagewell Software. Dana approved one and rejected the other, and both are still open. What should happen to a true-up once the controller has approved or rejected it?
answer: Our policy doesn't say what happens to a true-up after I've approved or rejected it, so don't clear either of the two Pagewell Software 6600 entries yourself. Keep both open and send them back to me as controller, and I'll decide how each one is closed out. The only related rule we have is that entries posted after close into a closed period come to me.

One correction to your rule: wire fees and analysis charges on the bank's fee schedule go to 7710 at any amount, and sweep interest goes to 7100. question: Every Paystream payout I saw had a report and a 1250 entry. When one of them is missing, should the payout go to the controller, or should staff hold it and chase Paystream?
answer: It goes to me, the controller. If a payout can't be tied exactly to the Paystream payout report (fees to 6310, refunds to 4090, chargebacks to 6320), I treat that as a variance, and variances come to me. Staff shouldn't hold it and chase Paystream on their own, and they shouldn't match it.

question: I could not replay this against any past item. Is this a convention you follow?
answer: No, we don't have that rule, and there's no standing approval for Skarvik Shipping or any other customer. A wire that's short because of bank charges gets matched with the charge booked to 7710 only when there's evidence for it: either the bank line says LESS CHGS or the remittance advice states the charge. Otherwise the shortfall goes to ar_lead, whatever the amount, and nothing is written off without my approval.

question: I could not replay this against any past item. Is this a convention you follow?
answer: No, we don't have a Skarvik-specific rule and we don't use a $5.00 threshold. Any unexplained short-pay goes to ar_lead, even $3. The only exception is when the shortfall is sender bank charges and the bank line says LESS CHGS or the remittance advice states it. Then we match the wire and post the charge to 7710.

question: Dana's standing approval depends on the Ledgerlane remittance showing the 1.25% fee, and the system cannot check that yet. Can the Ledgerlane remittance be loaded as a document so these wires clear automatically when the deduction is exactly 1.25%?
answer: That Varnholt/Ledgerlane rule and Dana's standing approval aren't part of our policy, so don't set up any auto-clear for them. For now, send every Varnholt Biosciences wire with a Ledgerlane deduction to me, whether or not a remittance is loaded and whether or not it's exactly 1.25%. Nothing gets booked to 6310 on these without my approval.
